name: Governance & ownership
definition: Records that establish the business entity, ownership, formal authority, governance structure, or major company decisions.
accountability_cue: The owners, directors, officers, or people responsible for the company's legal identity and formal authority would need this to be correct.
applicability_when: Use for entity formation, ownership, formal authority, governance actions, and durable company-level decisions that are not better owned by a specific operating function.
sensitivity_note: These records can expose ownership, signatures, authority, identity, corporate structure, financing authority, or other consequential company information.
examples: articles or certificate of incorporation | shareholder or ownership register | director or officer register | bylaws or governing rules | board or shareholder resolution | signing-authority record | major ownership-change record
review_triggers: incorporation or restructuring | ownership change | director or officer change | authority or signing change | new, amended, or revoked governance document | major company decision requiring formal record

name: Finance, accounting & tax
definition: Accounting books, transaction evidence, banking, receivables and payables, expenses, reconciliations, financial reporting, tax, and financial-remittance records.
accountability_cue: The person responsible for the books, cash, reporting, tax, or transaction evidence would need this to be correct.
applicability_when: Use when the record's primary purpose is to evidence, record, reconcile, report, pay, collect, remit, or support a financial or tax transaction or obligation.
sensitivity_note: Financial and tax records can expose account details, prices, margins, payroll information, tax identifiers, transactions, balances, and other high-impact business data.
examples: sales invoice | purchase invoice | receipt | bank statement | general ledger export | reconciliation | expense record | accounts receivable or payable report | tax return or filing support | payroll remittance record
review_triggers: month or year close | transaction corrected or reversed | bank or account change | tax filing or assessment | reconciliation exception | payment or collection issue | retention requirement reached under the applicable authority
related_categories: osbrt.customers_revenue | osbrt.vendors_procurement | osbrt.people_workforce | osbrt.assets_facilities | osbrt.inventory_supplies | osbrt.governance_ownership

name: Customers & revenue
definition: Records that define, develop, manage, or document customer relationships, commercial opportunities, sales commitments, and ongoing customer accounts.
accountability_cue: The person responsible for the customer relationship, sale, commercial commitment, or account would need this to be correct.
applicability_when: Use for customer and sales records whose main purpose is the commercial relationship rather than financial transaction evidence or execution of a specific job.
sensitivity_note: Customer records may contain personal information, pricing, commercial terms, correspondence, service history, or confidential customer information.
examples: lead or opportunity record | proposal | quote | customer master agreement | customer correspondence | pricing or commercial terms | account note | renewal or recurring-service record
review_triggers: new lead or customer | proposal or quote revision | agreement signed, amended, renewed, or ended | customer ownership or contact change | pricing or service change | account escalation or closure

name: Vendors & procurement
definition: Records used to source, evaluate, select, order from, manage, and communicate with suppliers and service providers.
accountability_cue: The person responsible for the supplier relationship, purchase decision, order, or procurement process would need this to be correct.
applicability_when: Use for supplier and procurement records whose main purpose is selecting, ordering from, or managing a vendor rather than recording the resulting financial transaction or managing a technology system.
sensitivity_note: Vendor records may contain pricing, negotiated terms, contact information, account references, banking or payment details, and commercially sensitive correspondence.
examples: supplier profile | supplier quote | purchase order | supplier agreement | price list | procurement comparison | credit or return authorization | receiving exception | vendor correspondence
review_triggers: new or terminated supplier | price or term change | purchase order issued or changed | supplier agreement renewed or amended | delivery or quality issue | vendor ownership or contact change

name: People & workforce
definition: Employment, contractor, role, compensation-administration, time, training, performance, and other workforce records about people working for or with the business.
accountability_cue: The person responsible for the worker relationship, role, employment administration, or workforce obligation would need this to be correct.
applicability_when: Use for records whose primary purpose is the working relationship or workforce administration. Payroll journals and remittance evidence remain Finance, accounting & tax when their main purpose is financial reporting or remittance.
sensitivity_note: Workforce records commonly contain identity, compensation, tax, banking, performance, health, schedule, disciplinary, or other sensitive personal information.
examples: employment agreement | contractor agreement | role description | employee or contractor profile | timesheet or attendance record | training record | performance record | benefit-enrolment administration | leave or accommodation administration
review_triggers: hire or contract start | role or compensation change | training or credential change | leave or accommodation change | performance or disciplinary event | worker departure | policy or benefit administration change

name: Projects, jobs & delivery
definition: Records that define, execute, change, approve, evidence, complete, or hand off specific customer work, projects, jobs, engagements, or deliverables.
accountability_cue: The person accountable for delivering the specific piece of work would need this to be correct.
applicability_when: Use when the record's primary purpose is execution or delivery of a defined job, project, engagement, or deliverable rather than the general customer relationship or a recurring company procedure.
sensitivity_note: Delivery records may contain customer information, locations, specifications, pricing, approvals, photos, schedules, or confidential project material.
examples: work order | statement of work | project scope | delivery plan | change order | field record | customer approval | project photo | completion record | handoff package
review_triggers: project or job opened | scope or schedule change | change order | milestone or approval | delivery issue | completion or cancellation | handoff or warranty transition

name: Operations & procedures
definition: Recurring operating procedures, checklists, schedules, instructions, quality methods, and routine process records used to run the business consistently.
accountability_cue: The person responsible for how a recurring business process is performed would need this to be correct.
applicability_when: Use for repeatable operating methods and process controls. Classify meeting notes, plans, and checklists by their actual subject when they belong more naturally to a customer, project, workforce, safety, technology, or strategy context.
sensitivity_note: Some operating material is routine; other procedures can expose security, internal controls, customer handling, facility practices, or proprietary methods.
examples: standard operating procedure | recurring checklist | operating schedule | work instruction | quality procedure | routine inspection checklist | process-control record | operations playbook
review_triggers: process change | quality issue | new equipment or system | policy or control change | recurring failure | scheduled procedure review | ownership change

name: Assets & facilities
definition: Records that identify, assign, operate, service, inspect, repair, warrant, or manage physical assets, equipment, vehicles, tools, premises, and facilities.
accountability_cue: The person responsible for the asset, equipment, vehicle, premises, or facility would need this to be correct.
applicability_when: Use when the record's main ongoing purpose is asset identity, custody, condition, operation, maintenance, warranty, inspection, or facility management. Purchase invoices remain Finance when their primary purpose is transaction evidence.
sensitivity_note: Asset and facility records can expose locations, serial numbers, access details, maintenance weaknesses, ownership, values, or security-related information.
examples: asset register | vehicle or equipment record | manual | warranty | maintenance record | repair history | inspection record | asset assignment | facility record | premises lease or occupancy record
review_triggers: purchase or disposal | assignment change | maintenance or repair | inspection | warranty change or expiry | facility move or lease change | loss, damage, or incident

name: Inventory & supplies
definition: Records used to identify, count, receive, store, issue, consume, reorder, adjust, or trace inventory, stock, materials, and recurring supplies.
accountability_cue: The person responsible for stock availability, movement, count accuracy, or material control would need this to be correct.
applicability_when: Use for inventory and supply control. Purchase invoices remain Finance, and supplier-selection records remain Vendors & procurement even when they relate to stocked items.
sensitivity_note: Inventory records range from routine stock counts to commercially sensitive cost, quantity, location, shrinkage, or controlled-material information.
examples: SKU or item master | stock count | receiving record | reorder record | inventory movement | usage record | inventory adjustment | bin or location record | material issue record
review_triggers: receipt or shipment | count or cycle count | reorder threshold | inventory adjustment | loss or damage | new or discontinued item | location or stocking-method change

name: Insurance, risk & incidents
definition: Insurance policies and certificates, claims, risk assessments, incident records, damage evidence, loss events, and other records primarily used to understand or manage business risk.
accountability_cue: The person responsible for insurance, risk response, claims, loss prevention, or incident handling would need this to be correct.
applicability_when: Use for insurance, claims, risk, and incident records. If the record exists primarily to satisfy a licence, statutory inspection, regulated safety program, or formal compliance obligation, Compliance, licences & safety may be primary instead.
sensitivity_note: Risk and incident records may contain personal information, allegations, injuries, damage, security details, insurer information, financial exposure, or legally consequential facts.
examples: insurance policy | certificate of insurance | claim record | incident report | damage photo | risk assessment | loss record | risk register | insurer correspondence
review_triggers: policy renewal or change | new claim or incident | damage or loss | risk assessment update | insurer request | claim closure | control or exposure change

name: Compliance, licences & safety
definition: Licences, permits, required certifications, regulated inspections, safety-program evidence, compliance records, and other material maintained primarily to demonstrate required permission or adherence.
accountability_cue: The person responsible for the licence, safety obligation, regulatory requirement, or compliance evidence would need this to be correct.
applicability_when: Use when the record's primary purpose is demonstrating or managing a specific legal, regulatory, licensing, safety, or professional requirement. Keep jurisdiction- and industry-specific rules as overlays rather than treating this taxonomy as the authority.
sensitivity_note: Compliance and safety records may contain personal, inspection, incident, location, certification, enforcement, or operational-risk information.
examples: business licence | permit | required certification | regulated inspection | safety training evidence | safety program record | compliance filing | corrective-action record | regulatory correspondence
review_triggers: licence or permit renewal | regulatory or policy change | inspection | certification expiry | incident or corrective action | new jurisdiction or line of business | regulator request

name: Technology, access & data
definition: Records that define, operate, administer, secure, recover, or document business systems, software, accounts, access, data handling, and technology services.
accountability_cue: The person responsible for the system, account, access model, configuration, data process, backup, or technology service would need this to be correct.
applicability_when: Use for technology ownership and administration. A software service agreement belongs here when its main purpose is the technology service; supplier payment evidence still belongs in Finance and general vendor selection may remain Vendors & procurement.
sensitivity_note: Technology records can reveal system architecture, account ownership, security controls, access paths, configuration, recovery methods, data locations, or other information that should be tightly controlled.
examples: system inventory | software subscription record | account ownership record | access procedure | configuration record | backup or recovery procedure | data-flow note | technology-service agreement | security-control record
review_triggers: new or retired system | vendor or subscription change | access-owner change | security event | configuration change | backup or recovery change | data-location or integration change

name: Marketing & brand
definition: Brand standards, creative assets, campaigns, content, advertising, media, messaging, publication, and other records used to present and promote the business.
accountability_cue: The person responsible for the brand, campaign, content, public messaging, or marketing channel would need this to be correct.
applicability_when: Use for brand and marketing material. Customer-specific proposals and commercial agreements remain Customers & revenue; final financial invoices remain Finance.
sensitivity_note: Published assets may be public, while unreleased campaigns, customer lists, budgets, performance data, credentials, or strategy can be commercially sensitive.
examples: brand guideline | logo or brand asset | campaign brief | advertisement | marketing photo or video | website copy | social content | media kit | publication asset
review_triggers: brand change | campaign launch or close | channel change | content correction | rights or usage change | asset superseded | major messaging or positioning change

name: Strategy & planning
definition: Business plans, forecasts, priorities, market or internal research, roadmaps, strategic decisions, and records whose main purpose is choosing or directing future action.
accountability_cue: The person responsible for deciding where the business is going, what it will prioritize, or how a major initiative will proceed would need this to be correct.
applicability_when: Use for forward-looking decision and planning material. Actual financial books remain Finance; a specific delivery plan belongs to Projects, jobs & delivery; recurring procedures belong to Operations & procedures.
sensitivity_note: Strategy records may reveal forecasts, priorities, competitive analysis, pricing direction, expansion plans, research, or other commercially sensitive decisions.
examples: business plan | forecast used for planning | strategic roadmap | priority plan | market research | decision memo | initiative brief | expansion plan | scenario analysis
review_triggers: planning cycle | major decision | forecast change | new initiative | market or competitor change | priority change | initiative closed or superseded

name: Knowledge & continuity
definition: Operational lessons, durable decision context, reference material, handoff notes, and other records whose main purpose is preserving what the business knows so work can continue across people and time.
accountability_cue: The person responsible for preserving reusable know-how, context, or continuity would need this to remain understandable and current.
applicability_when: Use only when preserving reusable knowledge or continuity is the record's primary purpose. Do not use it as a miscellaneous category for records that fit a real operating family.
sensitivity_note: Knowledge and handoff material can aggregate internal methods, customer context, access references, decisions, lessons, and other information that becomes sensitive when combined.
examples: lessons learned | handoff note | decision context | reference guide | continuity note | institutional knowledge record | process rationale | post-project learning summary
review_triggers: role handoff | major process or system change | lesson invalidated | reference source changes | decision superseded | business continuity review | knowledge owner changes
